name: @tellma/core
description: The Tellma app framework: the runtime a distribution's single-page app imports, split into entry points along its lazy-loading lines.

Re-baselined from 12.5 to 12.24 when the gate moved to the linked production measure (12.21 linked against 12.47 on the published bundle), keeping the same 0.03 of headroom. Raised from 12.24 to 16.59 for the client store and the tab bus: measured 12.21 before and 16.51 after on the linked measure (+4.30 KB, including the storage-fault fallback, the sweep result and the sweep-over-earlier-writes rule; 12.47 before and 16.82 after on the published-bundle measure), keeping the 0.08 of headroom it had on that measure, within the 9 KB share of spec 0025's primary services. The weight is TmClientStore (the mirror with its idle-rule views, readAll over partition ranges, put with the savedAt rule, patch in one transaction, the write guard, the three sweeps with their prefix messages, the re-read on another tab's commit and on a return from the back-forward cache, the boot step, the open with its 3 s timeout, memory fallback and versionchange close, and the boot record's read, patch and storage-event stream), TmTabBus over two BroadcastChannels (the queue until the slug is known, the per-user channel that follows the session, the back-forward-cache close and reopen, the envelope filter), TM_DOC_FORMATS and the browser seam. rxjs stays external, as Angular already ships it. Savings taken: one transaction helper serves every read, write and sweep; the mirror and the pending-write count are plain maps; the boot record reuses the boot script's parser and storage helpers. Raised from 16.59 to 20.28 for the cache refresher and the launch documents: measured 16.51 before and 20.19 after on the linked measure (+3.68 KB), keeping 0.09 of headroom; with the client store and the tab bus, spec 0025's primary services now weigh 7.98 KB of their 9 KB share. The weight is TmCacheRefresher (observe, refresh with its coalesced runs, the sync lock, the re-check inside it, the 2 s throttle and the one-transaction store of the answer, adopt with its preferences and locale patches, the cache.changed handler with its jitters, the membership-boundary timer with its backoff, the error routing and the sync telemetry), TmLaunchCache (the launch documents, the tenant entry with its cold sync, the lazily loaded entity lists with their stale and refused rules, and the user documents' background reads), TmLocks with its in-tab fallback, and the store's several-document write, its show-ahead and its re-read. Savings taken: put, patch and the several-document write share one write helper and one pending count; the refresher and the launch cache keep their state in private fields, which the minifier shortens; the four client tags are a list, not a map. Raised from 20.28 to 20.44 for the review fixes to the refresher and the store: measured 20.19 before and 20.35 after on the linked measure (+0.16 KB), keeping 0.09 of headroom; spec 0025's primary services now weigh 8.14 KB of their 9 KB share. The weight is a cold call's test of the launch documents themselves, a list's call that ends once a sync in flight reports the list's tag, the clamp on a sync stamp ahead of the clock, and an adoption kept shown over a sync's write. Savings taken: the shown updates live on the mirror entry, not in a map of their own (0.06 KB). Raised from 20.44 to 31 for the bootstrap, the derived routes, the URLs, the query codec and the route host: measured 20.36 before and 30.87 after on the linked measure (+10.51 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. The weight is TmUrls (the builders with the no-tenant rule, target, describe over the route table's order, preload with its once-per-chunk set, and the codec's parsers), the search query codec (the canonical printer, the lenient parser with its dropped-entry reports, the in/between escapes and the #d= base64url payload), the route table with its matchers, canMatch rules and section-aware leave check, the reuse strategy that creates every route anew on a change of tenant, TmRouteHost (the skeleton, the parallel chunk, Entities and cold-entry loads, the focus holds it gives back, the securable gate, the update check on a chunk failure, the page scope and the leave checks), the page skeleton, the four error views (offline, client-outdated, forbidden and not-found) and the not-found page, TmTitleStrategy, TmPageFocus with its in-place rule, the launch redirect with its page at /, the launch timer, TmApp with its navigation-failure view, the startup initializers with the Contracts chunk's load at idle, TmEntities, the interim platform text, TmUrlSerializer and bootstrapTellma. Savings taken: the shell stand-ins and the one placeholder page live in ./shell, loaded with import(). The not-found page, the launch page at / and the forbidden view stay here: moved into ./shell they took about 0.6 KB out of this measure, but ./shell loads with every first frame, so the first frame saved nothing, and they moved back (a chunk of their own, loaded only when they render, is left to the full re-split); the error view is one data-driven component; the six page-family hosts share one loader; the builders of the routed tenant and of forTenant are one class over a path prefix; the services keep their state in private fields, which the minifier shortens. The development error messages stay, since a developer acts on them. Split by spec, roughly: spec 0025's primary services 8.1 KB of their 9 KB share; TmEntities about 0.5 KB, which is spec 0029's share; spec 0024's own services the remaining 22.3 KB or so, against their 14 KB share in spec 0024. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. Raised from 31 to 36.5 for the preferences, page state, drafts, tree expansion and recents: measured 30.87 before and 36.00 after on the linked measure (+5.13 KB), the raise being that addition rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. The weight, by each part's marginal gzip in the measured bundle (approximate, as gzip shares its dictionary across parts): TmPreferences about 2.6 KB (the overlay over the stored bag, the parse-once cache with its invalid-value count, the deep-equal fallback delete, the 32 KB refusal, the cross-tab broadcast, the curated, write-behind and nav.recent schedules, the per-kind failure handling with the path-named and key-cap drops, the frozen hold, and the pagehide send with its 16 KB newest-first cut), TmDrafts about 0.8 KB (the debounced session-storage writes, the quota eviction into memory, the user check and the key listing), TmRecents with its routed-page and launcher seams about 0.6 KB, TmPageState about 0.5 KB (the LRU of 20, the entity and tenant stale marks and the access and languages watch), TmTreeExpansion about 0.5 KB (the pending operations over the stored ids, the debounced patch and the 500 cap), and the state dump, the store's document listing, the session partition at boot and the send's tenant about 0.1 KB. Savings taken: the draft-key helpers are shared with the session's sign-in sweep; recents reuse the page-state key for the path; the development checks sit behind ngDevMode, so production drops their messages; one dirty map per tenant serves the schedule, the flush, the retry and the pagehide send; the services keep their state in private fields, which the minifier shortens. Moving the key check's development guard to its call sites grew the measure by 0.13 KB and was not kept. Lowered from 36.5 to 34 after review, when the tab's memory and the recent pages left the primary, against spec 0025 §1, which places them in it: measured 36.00 before and 33.84 after on the linked measure (-2.16 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. TmDrafts, TmPageState and TmTreeExpansion moved to ./memory, which the page hosts load with them; TmRecents with its routed-page and launcher seams moved to ./recents, which the startup loads with import() after the first render; the drafts' storage and keys stay here for the session's sign-in sweep, and the state dump reads the services' parts through TM_STATE_PARTS instead of injecting them, so the dump costs about 0.13 KB on an app's first frame rather than 1.35. An app's first frame, measured as a split build of bootstrapTellma and provideTellma that follows the startup's import(), went from 33.60 KB to about 33.1 (33.14 in the entry and the shared chunk): the recents chunk imports TmPreferences from the primary, so the preferences and their flush engine stay on the first frame with everything else that chunk uses, and the move saves about 0.5 KB there. TmPreferences stays here, about 2.5 KB, and the startup creates it, so its receiver hears the other tabs from the first frame: its overlay and receiver are read before first render; moving its flush engine out is left to the full re-split. The second review's fixes (the startup's preferences and recents loader, and the refused write's revert) measure 33.82 KB on the linked measure, so the ceiling stays 34. Split by spec, roughly: spec 0025's primary services now about 11.0 KB of their 9 KB share, with 3.84 KB more in ./memory and ./recents; TmEntities about 0.5 KB, spec 0029's share; spec 0024's own services about 22.3 KB. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. Raised from 34 to 38.5 for localization, the strings, server text and the theme, which landed after the preferences and page state: measured 33.82 before and 38.49 after on the linked measure (+4.67 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. Before the preferences and page state, it measured 30.87 before and 35.61 after (+4.74 KB); its review fixes (a queue per tenant in the locale write, the tenant read from the address before the first navigation, the boot record following every settled language) measured 35.83 (+0.22 KB), and its second review fixes 35.45 (-0.38 KB): the locale write, with the latest choices per tenant it owns, the retry on a backoff and the rebase onto a landed result, moved into a chunk of its own that the first change saved in a tenant loads with import(), budgeted alone under lazyChunkBudgetsInKb (1.50 KB against 2, the measure rounded up to the next 0.5 KB), so the first frame does not carry it; the tab-bus switch message and the route host's wait for the tenant's language stay here. The weight is TmLocalization (every member of the language, the regional formats, the calendar and the zones as signals over the launch documents, the boot record and the client metadata; the load-then-apply switch with its linked language and calendar; the overlay of the locale write's choices once loaded; the document and Transloco wiring; the message resolver with its English fallback, development warning and bidi strip; the device-zone re-read and the four telemetry events), the resolution rules (the region, the canonical digits extension, the private-use language subtag and the once-per-tag browser check with its two fallbacks), TmServerText, the calendar-aware argument formatter, the string loader with its collision rule, the English platform table, the theme glue with theme-color, the provideTellma wiring of the library tokens and the request locale, and the twelve directional platform icons (about 0.3 KB of lucide data, within the 4 KB icon share). Savings taken: the development errors and warnings sit behind the build-time ngDevMode flag, which a production build folds away with their text (0.15 KB); the interim platform text is gone, its resolver being TmLocalization's; the route error views carry keys only, their English living once in the English table; the locale write loads only when a change is saved. Split by spec, roughly: spec 0025's primary services about 11.0 KB of their 9 KB share; TmEntities about 0.5 KB, spec 0029's share; the platform icon data 0.3 KB of its 4 KB share; spec 0024's own services the remaining 26.7 KB or so, against their 14 KB share. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. Kept at 38.5 when the primary was reviewed for a split into entry points by spec, because an app's start reaches nearly all of it. An app over the built package that imports only bootstrapTellma, provideTellma, tmEnglish, tmFeature and tmMetadataLoaders, bundled with code splitting as an app build bundles it, carried 37.79 KB of the primary on its first frame, against the 38.49 measured here. What it left out was TmServerText (about 0.3 KB), the state dump (about 0.1 KB), the declaration functions that features call (about 0.2 KB together) and tmPreferenceKey; each is needed at start once its consumers land (the shell, the attention surfaces, the error presenter and the support tools), so moving it to an entry point of its own would save nothing on the first frame. Neither would any family of services: provideTellma, the startup and the route host reach the HTTP layer, the session, localization, the URLs with the search query codec, the route table, the client store, the tab bus, the cache refresher, the launch cache, the preferences and the entity summaries at start, and an entry point the primary imports statically loads with it. One saving was real: the primary ships as one module, so TmDecimals' frozen helpers stayed on every app's first frame, used or not, until a pure annotation let a bundler drop them. That took the first frame to 37.10 KB (-0.69 KB), and a tree-shaking check holds it; this measure counts every export, so it stays 38.49. Split by spec, on two bases. On this gate's measure (38.49 KB), at the proportions below: spec 0024's own services about 25.5 KB against their 14 KB share, spec 0025's primary services about 12.1 KB against their 9 KB share, TmEntities about 0.5 KB of spec 0029's share, and spec 0026's seams about 0.3 KB. In an Acme production build, which compiles the primary from its sources and so drops what no import reaches (each family's minified code, found through the build's source map, gzipped alone and scaled to the 35.93 KB the primary's code weighs there together): spec 0024 about 23.8 KB, spec 0025 about 11.3, TmEntities about 0.45 and the seams about 0.26. Nothing moved between the two: the bases differ. The earlier figures in this note (spec 0024 about 26.7 KB, spec 0025 about 11.0) are on this gate's measure, and spec 0024's was the residual left after the other shares and the icon data, so it also held spec 0026's seams and the exports boot does not reach, TmDecimals' helpers among them. Raised from 38.5 to 42.5 for the entity registry: measured 38.49 before and 42.35 after on the linked measure (+3.86 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. The weight is TmPermissions (can, filtered, allows over the operation table with the details page, activate and model actions, disabledReason with the tenant's ReadOnly and Frozen states, sensitive, label through the securables section, and the memo per member and argument), which the route host's securable gate asks before a page renders; TmDisplayNames (the plan per entity and shape, the slot, number, date, separator, fallback and bidi rules, label over a cacheable entity's list and the held rows with their 5,000-row LRU and scope clearing, remember, rememberRelated and the per-frame resolve queue) and tm-display-name, which the eager shell and the attention bell read synchronously on the first frame; tmRowsToObjects, the TmEntities load with its telemetry, the development guards' messages and the entity strings. Savings taken: the descriptors, named enums, path resolution, the traversal rule and the display names' background reads live in the tm-entity-model chunk, which TmEntities.load() imports with the Entities chunk, so none of it is on the first frame; it is budgeted alone under lazyChunkBudgetsInKb (2.09 KB against 2.5, the measure rounded up to the next 0.5 KB); moving the reads there took 0.15 KB off this measure; the services keep their state in private fields, which the minifier shortens. With the chunk, spec 0029's primary share weighs about 5.95 KB of its 6 KB, of which 3.86 KB is on the first frame. Its first review's fixes (the select helper the golden shares, and resolve skipping the ids a loaded cacheable list holds) measure 42.39, and the chunk 2.07 with the segment-by-segment traversal walk, so the ceilings stay. Merged with the report stack, the primary still measures 42.39 KB, so its ceiling stays at 42.5, that figure rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. Raised from 42.5 to 45 for the shortcut registry and the shell frame's seams, which landed after the entity registry: measured 42.39 before and 44.52 after on the linked measure (+2.13 KB, the same addition its own branch measured before the entity registry, 38.49 to 40.62), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB, within the 5 KB share spec 0027 gives the primary. Every part is on the first frame: TmShortcuts is the one keydown listener, which the shell registers Mod+K, Mod+/ and the pin key with at its first render, and through which the primary's page actions and support tools register theirs (the dispatch with its skip, field, Option and modal rules; the family, grid, browser and live checks with the parsed-combination model; TM_RESERVED_SHORTCUTS, TM_BROWSER_KEYS and the registry's copy of the grid's modified keys, which keeps the grid's binding table off the first frame, about 1.97 KB if it were imported); TmShellMain is what the primary's error presenter calls when a tenant is unavailable; TmShell and TM_SHELL_LAYOUT are read by the shell and the banners at first render. Savings taken: the refusal messages exist only behind the build-time ngDevMode flag, which a production build folds away with their text; the busy check asks the overlay layer's probe rather than injecting TmBusyOverlay, which would create its host; tmSearchNormalize, which spec 0027 §1 places here, is the entry point ./search-normalize, since nothing on the first frame matches text. The primary's 50 KB total is not reached. Kept at 45 for the leader tab, which landed after the shortcut registry: measured 44.52 before and 44.81 after on the linked measure (+0.29 KB, about the addition its own branch measured before the entity registry, 38.49 to 38.77), within the ceiling, so no raise. The weight is TmLeader (isLeader, hubStatus and events() over a Subject, with the internal setters the election writes), TM_LEADER_DOCUMENTS and the store's extra formats built from it, the startup's loader of ./leader after the first render with the one helper it now shares with the recent pages' loader, and the state dump's leader member. Each is on the first frame for a reason: TmLeader is what the shell's connection state and the attention surfaces, as they land, read at their first render, before the election has loaded, so it lives where they can read it from the start and the election writes into it; the store's boot step reads the formats of the leader documents with every other format; the loader is the startup's. Savings taken: the election, the probes and steals, the leader's connection, relay, leader-document reads and degraded polling, which spec 0025 §1 places in the primary, live in ./leader (3.84 KB), which the startup loads with import() after the first render, so they leave the first frame; the leader's lock goes straight to the browser's LockManager rather than through a new mode of TmLocks; the two lazy loaders of the startup share one helper. Split by spec, roughly: spec 0025's primary services about 12.4 KB of their 9 KB share, with 7.91 KB more in ./memory, ./recents and ./leader. Raised from 45 to 47 for the page context and the page actions: measured 44.52 before and 46.62 after on the linked measure (+2.10 KB), then 46.79 once every page route got its default context (+2.27 KB in all), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB, within the 6 KB share spec 0026 gives the primary, and under the primary's 50 KB total. The weight is the page-context registry (the contexts and actions of every page scope, the merged action list with replacement and place order, current, overlays and top), the dispatcher (the search from the top context down, the disabled, busy and confirmation gates with the polite announcement, the run with its running set, the usage event), the effect that keeps the top context's shortcuts registered, TmPageContexts, TmPageActions and the scope provider, tmSerializePageContext with its masks, and the route host's default context on every page route, titled through the title strategy and registered anew when a reused route shows another entity. Savings taken: TmConfirm loads with import() at the first destructive question and TmLocalization is read only then; the development checks are module functions behind the build-time ngDevMode flag, so a production build drops them with their messages (0.18 KB). Lowered from 47 to 46.5 when tmSerializePageContext with its masks and snapshot types left the primary for ./page-snapshot, against spec 0026 §1, which places it here: measured 46.79 before and 46.29 after on the linked measure (-0.50 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB. Nothing on the first frame reads a snapshot; the support dump and a future assistant load it with import(). Raised from 46.5 to 47 on merging with the leader tab and the entity work that landed alongside: measured 46.29 before the merge and 46.74 after it on the linked measure (+0.45 KB, their own additions to the primary), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB, 3.26 KB under the primary's 50 KB total. Raised from 47 to 48.5 for spec 0028's primary members, on merging them: measured 46.74 before and 48.24 after on the linked measure (+1.50 KB of spec 0028's 2.5 KB primary share, as on their own base, 44.81 to 46.31), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB, 1.76 KB under the primary's 50 KB total. The weight is TmBanners (the precedence and the pager, dismissal per tab and per scope, the input-idle gate on the row's height with its immediate cases, the ungated head the banner host announces from, the queued-to-shown timing and the development checks), TmInputIdle (the five passive capture listeners and one self-re-arming timer), the offline banner's source with its 5 s threshold, TM_ATTENTION_DOCUMENTS with the inbox's pollWhile, the launch cache's inbox document, the wifi-off icon and the offline string. Each is on the first frame for a reason: the offline source runs from startup in every shell and raises banners through TmBanners, and spec 0024's time-zone prompt and the banner row wait on TmInputIdle; the attention documents are registered with the store's formats at its boot step. Savings taken: the banner host, its live region and its announcement timer live in ./attention (1.08 KB), not here; the gate is one settle routine over plain fields rather than effects; the input-idle handler only stamps the time, so one timer serves a stream of pointer moves; the development checks' messages fold away with ngDevMode; the update banner's source is not here yet (its owner adds it). The two reviews added 0.08 KB of that: the assignments document is no longer registered until the server serves it (-0.02); the leader documents are read once per name, with a development check for a name registered twice; a new banner that outranks the user's page moves the pager to it; the input-idle clock reads the monotonic clock; and the store's idle-time sweep skips an app that has ended; then the assignments summary is a plain store format until its leader read lands, the banners' settle step runs untracked and times on the monotonic clock, and the election asks each registration's own pollWhile. The figures that follow are on the published-bundle measure. Raised from 1.5 to 4.5 for the distribution API: measured 1.26 before and 4.32 after (+3.06 KB). The weight is the merge rule behind TM_APP_DECLARATIONS (about 2.4 KB: keys, overrides, coded-report patches, hide and the app-bar rules, each problem recorded with its facts), then tmFeature and the declaration functions, provideTellma, the metadata loaders and TM_CLIENT_METADATA. Savings taken: the merge keeps its state in private fields, which the minifier shortens (0.11 KB), and the config check, which the spec places in the primary, lives in the lazy ./config-check instead. The primary's ceiling keeps growing towards the sum of its shares as each owner lands. Raised from 4.5 to 6.5 for the session and launch: measured 4.32 before and 6.34 after (+2.02 KB). The weight is TmSession (the profile cookie decoder, check, signIn with the sign-in mark and step-up parameters, and the mark consumption that sweeps a previous user's drafts), the session guard and paths (the expiry's cookie delete, reload and sign-in loop guard), TmLaunch with its router subscription, tmSingleLiveTenant, and the shared web-storage and boot-record helpers; the boot script's own logic and page builder are not in the primary, since the script runs before the app and hands its result over on window.__tmBoot. Savings taken: the session's writable state lives in TmSessionPaths instead of a third injectable, and check() compares the decoder-built profiles as JSON instead of member by member (0.05 KB together); the sign-in error messages stay, since a developer acts on them. Raised from 6.5 to 12.5 for the HTTP layer: measured 6.34 before and 12.27 after (+5.93 KB), within the 14 KB share of this spec's own services. The weight is TmHttpApi (the call pipeline: tenant routing, the Contracts lookups, the gates, the watchdog, retries with abortable waits, the status table, the outdated-client verdict with the worker cap, download streaming, the XHR upload, keepalive sends and the blob fetcher), the wire helpers (problem, Retry-After, version tags, step-up, Content-Disposition, trace ids, SemVer precedence), TmApiError, the reachability probe and the browser and service seams. Savings taken: fetch, XHR and blob fetches share one judging path (response check, observers, status table, verdict) instead of one per transport; the retry table is data driven; the layer keeps its state in private fields, which the minifier shortens. The development error messages stay, since a developer acts on them. Raised from 48.5 to 49.5 for spec 0027's primary members, on merging them: the navigation registry, the core feature's launcher sections and entries, the pins model's keys and the launcher's provider seam. Measured 48.24 before and 50.09 after on the linked measure (+1.85 KB), then 49.40 once two parts of the HTTP layer that no first-frame call needs moved into lazy chunks (-0.69 KB), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.5 KB, 0.60 KB under the primary's 50 KB total; with the shortcut registry and the shell frame's seams, spec 0027's primary share now weighs about 3.9 KB of its 5 KB. The weight, by cutting each part out of the built bundle: TmNavigation with its constants about 1.38 KB (the candidates derived from entities, pages, coded reports and feature entries, the permission rule with any-of requires and the settings categories' rule for core.settings, visibleWhen over the distribution document with the once-only report of a predicate that throws, the order and localized-label sort, the section and search-only split, byHref, and resolve with the route-owner, permission and core-route checks), the core sections and six entries about 0.22 and their place in the core feature about 0.05, their English labels about 0.05, tmPinsKey and tmPinnedBarVisibleKey with the shape check about 0.07, and TM_LAUNCHER_PROVIDERS about 0.01. Each is on the first frame for a reason: spec 0027 §1 places the registry, the pins keys and the launcher token here, and the eager pinned bar reads resolve, byHref, the entry labels and both keys at its first render. Savings taken, on the first frame: the core entries' search synonyms are the launcher's own strings, which its deferred chunk registers when it loads (0.04 KB); the default and core entry icons are names, so no glyph data joins the first frame (0.92 KB if registered here). Measure only, not the first frame: the pinned bar's item rules (validation and caps, capture, the current-pin and label rules and the id generator) live with the bar in ./shell, which the bar reads at its first render, so they return to every tenant's first frame through the modulepreloaded ./shell once the bar lands; the launcher's term reader leaves the first frame only as it lands in the deferred launcher chunk. Together they took 0.89 KB off this measure. Moved out to keep the primary under its total, against spec 0024's placement of the whole HTTP layer here, since no first-frame call needs either: the outdated-client verdict's build rules (the SemVer order and the first-older window) into the tm-api-verdict chunk, which the layer imports at the first 412 client-outdated or 404 route-not-found answer and which, when it cannot load, leaves the builds to the worker's update check as for unordered builds (-0.34 KB); and the file transfers (a download's streamed read with its Content-Disposition name, and an upload's XMLHttpRequest send with its progress and watchdog) into the tm-api-transfer chunk, which the layer imports at a download's answer or an upload's send and whose failure to load fails the attempt as a network failure would (-0.35 KB). Each chunk is budgeted alone under lazyChunkBudgetsInKb: tm-api-verdict 0.51 KB and tm-api-transfer 0.75 KB, each against 1. Kept at 49.5 for the HTTP layer at the app's end, which landed after the lazy verdict and transfers: measured 49.39 before and 49.46 after on the linked measure (+0.07 KB; the gzip 9 cap 49.30 before and 49.36 after, against 50), within the ceiling, so no raise. Savings taken: the end joins the caller's and the session's cancellation in one test with one throw (0.01 KB), and the verdict checks the end once, after both of its waits. A shared helper for the cancelled attempt measured 0.03 KB more, since gzip favours the repeated literal, and was not kept. Raised from 49.5 to 49.89 for spec 0024's service worker updates, error presentation and session paths, on merging them: measured 49.46 before and 49.88 after on the linked measure (+0.42 KB; the gzip 9 cap 49.36 before and 49.78 after, against 50), the ceiling being that measurement rounded up to the next 0.01 KB, with no headroom, since the rest of the room under the 50 KB cap is reserved for queued work. The weight is TmSessionPaths' state, its bus routing from startup, the chunk loader with its fallbacks (a reload with the stale cookie deleted, or the root), the once-per-tab expiry guard and TmSession.signOut; the TM_API_UPDATES seam, a check only, which loads ./updates on the first check; the one loader of ./errors that TM_SYNC_ERRORS and the route error view share; the route error view's client-outdated Reload, which renders the error views' inline state once ./errors loads and hands it a Reload clicked before then, and reloads plainly when ./errors does not load; and the support dump's list of the drafts session storage holds while the drafts service is not loaded. Savings taken, each against spec 0024 §1, which places them in the primary: the sign-out, expiry, changed-user and signed-out flows with their dialog, overlays, strings and re-check triggers live in the tm-session-flows chunk, budgeted alone under lazyChunkBudgetsInKb (3.04 KB against 3.5) and preloaded after the first render; the error presenter with its table, dialogs and tenant-state view lives in ./errors; TmUpdates with the worker registration, the Trusted Types policy and the update banner lives in ./updates. Moving the re-check triggers into the chunk took 0.05 KB off this measure. budgetNotes._: Ceilings are ratchets. Any raise belongs here with its reason; a raise with no note is a bug.
